Manages dynamic character strings via allocators and seamlessly integrates StringView views.

In the module core, the class ara::core::BasicString provides a memory-allocator-aware string implementation based on the C++ PMR standard [SWS_CORE_03005]. It handles dynamic buffer management, supports operations from reservation to appending, and interacts seamlessly with StringView. As an essential safety-relevant constraint, erroneous accesses are reported not by STL exceptions, but by AUTOSAR-specific violations such as IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation [SWS_CORE_03063].

Context

In module core of the AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform, the class ara::core::BasicString represents an implementation of the C++ standard type std::pmr::basic_string (defined in the header file #include "ara/core/string.h"). It represents a dynamic string class template that is parameterized via the type parameter Allocator [SWS_CORE_03005]. Compared to the general standard [basic.string], the AUTOSAR specification exhibits significant specializations: The character type traits_type is bindingly fixed to std::char_traits<char> [SWS_CORE_03003], size_type is specialized to std::size_t [SWS_CORE_03012], and charT is replaced by value_type [SWS_CORE_03004]. Key interaction partners are the allocating memory manager (via allocator_type) and the reference class StringView, with which BasicString collaborates closely via direct conversion operators [SWS_CORE_03301] and constructors [SWS_CORE_03302].

Lifecycle

The lifecycle of an instance begins with its construction. In addition to the default construction [SWS_CORE_03024], a specific allocator can be explicitly passed [SWS_CORE_03025]. Strings can also be created from C strings [SWS_CORE_03029], substrings [SWS_CORE_03026], initializer lists [SWS_CORE_03032], iterators [SWS_CORE_03031], or views such as StringView [SWS_CORE_03302]. Copy operations [SWS_CORE_03020] request new dynamic memory via the allocator. For resource-efficient transfers of ownership, a move construction is available, which is declared as noexcept [SWS_CORE_03022].

During its lifetime, the instance manages its memory area autonomously. The content can be modified via assignments ([SWS_CORE_03021], [SWS_CORE_03084]), size adjustments via resize ([SWS_CORE_03058], [SWS_CORE_03059]), or resetting by means of clear [SWS_CORE_03057]. Two strings can be swapped efficiently via swap, which is conditionally exception-safe [SWS_CORE_03412]. At the end of the lifecycle, the destructor ~BasicString() [SWS_CORE_03038] releases the allocated memory via the assigned allocator. Regarding concurrency, BasicString does not provide thread synchronization of its own; concurrent modifying accesses to the same instance therefore require external protection.

Usage Path

A typical usage path includes instantiation, optional buffer reservation, stepwise modification, and final read access or passing:

  • Creation: The instance is created, for example with explicit passing of an allocator instance [SWS_CORE_03025] or from an existing string view [SWS_CORE_03302].
  • Capacity reservation: To avoid repeated reallocations during successive text construction, buffer capacity can be requested in advance with reserve [SWS_CORE_03054].
  • Modification: Text contents are appended via append ([SWS_CORE_03076], [SWS_CORE_03308]) or operator+= ([SWS_CORE_03072], [SWS_CORE_03307]). Character-by-character insertion or replacement is performed via insert [SWS_CORE_03093] and replace [SWS_CORE_03106].
  • Reading and inspection: The content is read out via data [SWS_CORE_03070], the null-terminated pointer c_str [SWS_CORE_03069], element accesses via operator[] [SWS_CORE_03061], or conversion to StringView [SWS_CORE_03301].

Sequence diagram: Typical interaction sequence from initialization via buffer reservation and text modification to view conversion. Sources: [SWS_CORE_03025], [SWS_CORE_03054], [SWS_CORE_03308], [SWS_CORE_03301].

Error Scenarios

For invalid calls, the specification defines specific violation types instead of standard exceptions:

  • IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation: Triggered when a passed index or offset position exceeds the current size. This applies to indexed element access via at ([SWS_CORE_03063], [SWS_CORE_03064]), substring creation with substr [SWS_CORE_03345], range erasures via erase [SWS_CORE_03102], buffer copying by means of copy [SWS_CORE_03410], and positioned insert and replace operations ([SWS_CORE_03094], [SWS_CORE_03107]).
  • IsoStdLengthErrorViolation: Caused as soon as a requested string length or buffer expansion exceeds the maximum capacity max_size() [SWS_CORE_03053]. Relevant interfaces are reserve [SWS_CORE_03054], resize ([SWS_CORE_03058], [SWS_CORE_03059]), append [SWS_CORE_03078], assign [SWS_CORE_03088], insert [SWS_CORE_03095], and replace [SWS_CORE_03108].

Regarding exception safety, most allocating and modifying methods are designated as not exception safe, since memory shortages or faulty parameters can result in the failure of the operation. Exception guarantees are primarily provided by operations declared noexcept, such as move construction [SWS_CORE_03022] as well as conditionally move assignment [SWS_CORE_03023] and swap [SWS_CORE_03412]. The replacement of standard exceptions by IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation and IsoStdLengthErrorViolation is likely due to the platform-wide approach of deterministically mapping errors in safety-relevant execution environments.

This guide is based on the specification for ara::core::BasicString in AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform R25-11.

The assignment operator operator+= of class ara::core::BasicString ([SWS_CORE_03072] from #include "ara/core/string.h") synchronously appends the content of a passed BasicString instance to the current object. The functional semantics follow the corresponding usage in [basic.string] ([SWS_CORE_03072]). The call returns a reference to the modified instance (*this), enabling assignment chaining.

Regarding error handling, the operation is explicitly declared as "not exception safe" in the specification ([SWS_CORE_03072]). Specific error codes or notification mechanisms via DET or DEM are not defined for this element. Should an internal memory allocation fail, the method therefore provides no exception safety guarantee.

Regarding concurrency and constraints, it should be noted that the call modifies the state of the instance directly. Since the payload does not mention any synchronization mechanisms, concurrent read or write access to the same object across multiple threads is likely not thread-safe without external synchronization.

Together with further overloads of operator+=, the operator forms the interface for string appending, for instance for single characters ([SWS_CORE_03074]), raw character pointers ([SWS_CORE_03073]), initializer lists ([SWS_CORE_03075]), and StringView ([SWS_CORE_03307]). All of these modifying operators share the "not exception safe" property and complement the basic constructors of ara::core::BasicString ([SWS_CORE_03024], [SWS_CORE_03025]).

                      Error Handling and Exception Safety
                      

                      The element is specified as conditionally exception safe (conditionally exception safe) ([SWS_CORE_03024]). The semantic behavior and requirements correspond to the definitions of the ISO C++ standard in [basic.string].

This distinguishes the constructor from strictly exception-safe overloads such as [SWS_CORE_03025] or conditionally exception-safe variants such as [SWS_CORE_03024].

                                                                                  Usage and Semantics
                                                                                  

                                                                                  The member function append of class ara::core::BasicString ([SWS_CORE_03076]) from header file #include "ara/core/string.h" serves to synchronously append a complete string object str of type BasicString to the calling instance. The semantics follow the standardized C++ definition under [basic.string]; as return value, the function returns a reference to the modified object (*this) ([SWS_CORE_03076]).
                                                                                  


                                                                                  Error Handling and Boundary Conditions
                                                                                  

                                                                                  Regarding exception safety, the operation is explicitly classified as not exception safe ([SWS_CORE_03076]). Interpretation: If an error occurs during execution (for example, in case of insufficient memory), the state of the string is likely indeterminate, as no recovery guarantees are specified. In contrast to variants with position indices such as [SWS_CORE_03077] or [SWS_CORE_03309] (triggering IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation) or buffer size checks such as [SWS_CORE_03078] (triggering IsoStdLengthErrorViolation), [SWS_CORE_03076] defines no separate violations.
                                                                                  


                                                                                  Interplay and overloads
                                                                                  

                                                                                  The function is part of a family of overloads within ara::core::BasicString:
                                                                                  

                                                                                    

                                                                                  • Appending substrings via position and length specifications ([SWS_CORE_03077]).
                                                                                    • 

                                                                                  • Taking character arrays of type value_type* with defined length ([SWS_CORE_03078]) or as a null-terminated string ([SWS_CORE_03079]).
                                                                                    • 

                                                                                  • Repeated appending of single characters ([SWS_CORE_03080]) or assignment via std::initializer_list<value_type> ([SWS_CORE_03082]).
                                                                                    • 

                                                                                  • Integrating iterator ranges ([SWS_CORE_03081]) as well as string views via StringView ([SWS_CORE_03308]) and type-specific templates ([SWS_CORE_03309]).

                                                                                      function append [SWS_CORE_03077]
                                                                                      

                                                                                      BasicString & append (const BasicString &str, size_type pos, size_type n=npos);
                                                                                      

                                                                                      As per corresponding usage in [basic.string] except for the following deviations: 1. if (pos > str.size()) IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is raised instead of std:: out_of_range
                                                                                      

                                                                                      

                                                                                      

                                                                                      

                                                                                      

                                                                                      

                                                                                      

                                                                                      

                                                                                      
  AI-GENERATED
  unreviewed
  Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: e04fcf79dc67
  Provenance
  

                                                                                      

                                                                                      

                                                                                      The member function append of class ara::core::BasicString ([SWS_CORE_03077], declared in #include "ara/core/string.h") synchronously appends a substring of another BasicString instance str to the current object. The parameters pos and n (by default npos) determine the start index and the maximum number of characters within str. A reference to the modified target object (*this) is returned as the return value.
                                                                                      

                                                                                      Regarding semantics and interface behavior, the function follows the definition in [basic.string] of the C++ standard, but deviates in error handling: If pos > str.size() holds, a IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is triggered in accordance with [SWS_CORE_03077] (analogous to std::out_of_range). The specification explicitly classifies the operation as not exception safe, which is why no assurance of an unchanged or consistent object state is given in the event of an error.
                                                                                      

                                                                                      In the absence of documented synchronization mechanisms, concurrent calls on the same instance are likely not thread-safe. Further overloads are available in the module for alternative data sources: whole strings ([SWS_CORE_03076]), buffers and pointers ([SWS_CORE_03078], [SWS_CORE_03079]), character repetitions ([SWS_CORE_03080]), iterator pairs ([SWS_CORE_03081]), initializer lists ([SWS_CORE_03082]), and StringView objects ([SWS_CORE_03308], [SWS_CORE_03309]).

                                                                                          function append [SWS_CORE_03078]
                                                                                          

                                                                                          BasicString & append (const value_type *s, size_type n);
                                                                                          

                                                                                          As per corresponding usage in [basic.string] except for the following deviations: 1. charT replaced with value_type 2. if ( size() > n + max_size() ) IsoStdLengthErrorViolation is raised instead of std::length_error
                                                                                          

                                                                                          

                                                                                          

                                                                                          

                                                                                          

                                                                                          

                                                                                          

                                                                                          

                                                                                          
  AI-GENERATED
  unreviewed
  Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 30d65bf4c37d
  Provenance
  

                                                                                          

                                                                                          

                                                                                          The member function append of class ara::core::BasicString ([SWS_CORE_03078]) synchronously appends the first n characters of the passed character array s of type const value_type* to the existing string. As return value, the function returns a reference to the modified instance (BasicString&), which enables chaining consecutive calls. The declaration is available via header file #include "ara/core/string.h".
                                                                                          

  
                                                                                          The functional behavior follows the specification of std::basic_string::append according to [basic.string], but exhibits specific AUTOSAR deviations ([SWS_CORE_03078]):
                                                                                          
  
                                                                                            
    
                                                                                          • The template parameter charT is replaced by type value_type.
                                                                                            • 
    
                                                                                          • If the resulting length exceeds the capacity limit (condition size() > n + max_size()), the violation IsoStdLengthErrorViolation is triggered instead of a std::length_error.
                                                                                            • 
  
                                                                                          

  
                                                                                          Regarding execution safety, the operation is explicitly specified as not exception safe ([SWS_CORE_03078]). If an error or violation occurs during memory allocation or copying, the object does not guarantee a consistent intermediate state.
                                                                                          

  
                                                                                          The method complements the other overloads of append within ara::core::BasicString. These include appending complete instances ([SWS_CORE_03076]), substrings with bounds checking via IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation ([SWS_CORE_03077]), null-terminated strings ([SWS_CORE_03079]), sequences of identical characters ([SWS_CORE_03080]), iterator ranges ([SWS_CORE_03081]), initializer lists ([SWS_CORE_03082]), and StringView objects ([SWS_CORE_03308], [SWS_CORE_03309]).

                                                                                              The member function append of class ara::core::BasicString ([SWS_CORE_03079]) appends a null-terminated string of pointer type const value_type* to the existing string. The semantics correspond to the behavior from the C++ standard [basic.string], where charT is replaced by value_type. As return value, the synchronous function returns a reference to the calling object (BasicString&), which enables the chaining of successive operations.
                                                                                              


                                                                                              Regarding error handling and exception safety, the operation is explicitly classified as not exception safe ([SWS_CORE_03079]). In contrast to the overload with length specification [SWS_CORE_03078], which triggers a IsoStdLengthErrorViolation when the maximum length is exceeded, or substring overloads such as [SWS_CORE_03077] with IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation, this variant does not define any specific violation classes. It should be the caller's responsibility to ensure that the passed pointer s points to a valid, null-terminated character sequence.
                                                                                              


                                                                                              The function is part of a family of overloads for appending data in ara::core::BasicString:
                                                                                              

                                                                                                

                                                                                              • Appending complete or partial strings of the same type ([SWS_CORE_03076], [SWS_CORE_03077]),
                                                                                                • 

                                                                                              • Appending pointer prefixes with an explicit length restriction ([SWS_CORE_03078]),
                                                                                                • 

                                                                                              • Appending character repetitions ([SWS_CORE_03080]) or initializer lists ([SWS_CORE_03082]),
                                                                                                • 

                                                                                              • Processing iterator ranges ([SWS_CORE_03081]) as well as string views ([SWS_CORE_03308], [SWS_CORE_03309]).

                                                                                                  The member function append of ara::core::BasicString ([SWS_CORE_03080]) synchronously appends a specified count n of characters of type value_type (parameter c) to the existing string. It is provided via the header ara/core/string.h and returns a reference to the modified instance (*this), which enables chained calls.
                                                                                                  

                                                                                                  The functional behavior follows the definition of the C++ standard for [basic.string], where charT is replaced by value_type ([SWS_CORE_03080]). Regarding exception safety, the function is explicitly classified as not exception safe ([SWS_CORE_03080]). In contrast to other overloads such as [SWS_CORE_03077] or [SWS_CORE_03078], no specific runtime violations like IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation or IsoStdLengthErrorViolation are defined for this variant. Presumably, the method does not guarantee an unchanged state of the instance in case of an error.
                                                                                                  

                                                                                                  In the context of concurrency and thread safety, it must be noted that concurrent write accesses to the same instance of BasicString presumably must be synchronized externally. The function complements the other overloads of append in ara::core::BasicString, which cover appending complete strings ([SWS_CORE_03076]), subranges ([SWS_CORE_03077]), pointer buffers ([SWS_CORE_03078], [SWS_CORE_03079]), iterator ranges ([SWS_CORE_03081]), initializer lists ([SWS_CORE_03082]), or StringView objects ([SWS_CORE_03308], [SWS_CORE_03309]).

                                                                                                      function append [SWS_CORE_03081]
                                                                                                      

                                                                                                      template <class InputIterator> BasicString & append (InputIterator first, InputIterator last);
                                                                                                      

                                                                                                      As per corresponding usage in [basic.string]
                                                                                                      

                                                                                                      

                                                                                                      

                                                                                                      

                                                                                                      

                                                                                                      

                                                                                                      

                                                                                                      

                                                                                                      
  AI-GENERATED
  unreviewed
  Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: e0fa0fe8b021
  Provenance
  

                                                                                                      

                                                                                                      

                                                                                                      Usage and Semantics
                                                                                                      

                                                                                                      
The template member function append of class ara::core::BasicString is provided via the header file ara/core/string.h [SWS_CORE_03081]. It synchronously appends a sequence of characters bounded by the iterator pair first and last of category InputIterator to the existing string [SWS_CORE_03081]. The functional behavior complies with the corresponding definition in [basic.string] of the C++ standard [SWS_CORE_03081]. The operation returns a reference to the modified BasicString object (*this) as return value [SWS_CORE_03081].

                                                                                                      


                                                                                                      Error Handling and Exception Safety
                                                                                                      

                                                                                                      
For this function, exception safety is explicitly specified as not exception safe [SWS_CORE_03081]. In the event of an error—for example, if dynamic memory is exhausted during buffer expansion—the instance should remain in an invalid state according to interpretation. Specific AUTOSAR violations such as IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation or IsoStdLengthErrorViolation are not defined for this iterator overload, unlike other overloads of method [SWS_CORE_03077], [SWS_CORE_03078].

                                                                                                      


                                                                                                      Interplay in the module
                                                                                                      

                                                                                                      
The function is part of an extensive group of overloads for appending data to ara::core::BasicString:

                                                                                                      

                                                                                                        

                                                                                                      • Appending complete or partial strings of type BasicString [SWS_CORE_03076], [SWS_CORE_03077].
                                                                                                        • 

                                                                                                      • Appending character arrays with length specification or null-terminated character sequences [SWS_CORE_03078], [SWS_CORE_03079].
                                                                                                        • 

                                                                                                      • Repeated appending of single characters [SWS_CORE_03080] as well as adoption from std::initializer_list [SWS_CORE_03082].
                                                                                                        • 

                                                                                                      • Integration of modern string views via StringView or generic view types [SWS_CORE_03308], [SWS_CORE_03309].
                                                                                                        • 

                                                                                                      

                                                                                                      
The iterator variant [SWS_CORE_03081] thereby offers maximum flexibility for integrating arbitrary generic data sources.

                                                                                                          The member function append of class ara::core::BasicString synchronously appends the characters of an initializer list of type std::initializer_list<value_type> to the existing string object [SWS_CORE_03082]. The behavior follows the semantics of [basic.string] from the C++ standard with the difference that charT is replaced by value_type [SWS_CORE_03082]. The call modifies the instance directly and returns a reference to the object, enabling method chaining.
                                                                                                          

                                                                                                          Regarding error handling, the function is classified as not exception-safe (not exception safe) [SWS_CORE_03082]. Unlike related overloads such as [SWS_CORE_03077] or [SWS_CORE_03078], this variant does not define specific violations such as IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation or IsoStdLengthErrorViolation. Interpretation: If the internal memory allocation fails, the object presumably remains in an undefined state. Since the internal state is modified, a concurrent call without external synchronization is likely to result in data races.
                                                                                                          

                                                                                                          In interplay within ara::core::BasicString, the function is part of a group of related append operations. It complements overloads for entire strings ([SWS_CORE_03076]), subranges ([SWS_CORE_03077]), pointers to strings ([SWS_CORE_03078], [SWS_CORE_03079]), repeated single characters ([SWS_CORE_03080]), iterator ranges ([SWS_CORE_03081]), and StringView instances ([SWS_CORE_03308], [SWS_CORE_03309]).

                                                                                                              use
                                                                                                              

                                                                                                              The synchronous member function append of class ara::core::BasicString appends the characters of a passed string view (StringView sv) to the existing string [SWS_CORE_03308]. The interface is included via header #include "ara/core/string.h" [SWS_CORE_03308]. It returns a reference to the calling instance (BasicString &), allowing multiple modifications to be chained [SWS_CORE_03308]. The functional semantics follow the corresponding specification in C++ [basic.string] [SWS_CORE_03308].
                                                                                                              


                                                                                                              Error Handling and Exception Safety
                                                                                                              

                                                                                                              In AUTOSAR, the function is explicitly specified as not exception safe ("not exception safe") [SWS_CORE_03308]. Specific error codes, DET or DEM messages, and explicit AUTOSAR violations are not specified for this call, whereas related overloads such as [SWS_CORE_03077] or [SWS_CORE_03309] trigger a IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation on index overflow and [SWS_CORE_03078] triggers a IsoStdLengthErrorViolation on length overflow.
                                                                                                              


                                                                                                              Concurrency and Interaction
                                                                                                              

                                                                                                              Since append directly modifies the state of the invoked string object, concurrent access by multiple threads to the same instance without external synchronization is likely not thread-safe. The method is grouped with further append variants of ara::core::BasicString, which allow appending complete BasicString instances [SWS_CORE_03076], C strings [SWS_CORE_03079], repeated single characters [SWS_CORE_03080], as well as iterator ranges [SWS_CORE_03081] or initializer lists [SWS_CORE_03082].

                                                                                                                  use
                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                  The template function append of class ara::core::BasicString ([SWS_CORE_03309]) from the header file #include "ara/core/string.h" serves to synchronously append a subrange of an object t to the calling string. The behavior is oriented toward the ISO C++ specification [basic.string]. The parameter pos specifies the start index in the source object, while n determines the maximum number of characters to append (default value npos). A reference to the modified string object (*this) is provided as return value. Interpretation: The passed object t is likely interpreted internally as a string view sv.
                                                                                                                  


                                                                                                                  Error handling
                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                  AUTOSAR defines a specific deviation from the C++ standard for this function: If the specified position is greater than the size of the source range (pos > sv.size()), a IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is triggered instead of std::out_of_range ([SWS_CORE_03309]). The semantic description of this violation corresponds to that of std::out_of_range.
                                                                                                                  


                                                                                                                  Restrictions and Exception Safety
                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                  The operation is explicitly classified as not exception safe in the specification ([SWS_CORE_03309]). In the event of occurring errors, a stable retention of the previous state is therefore not guaranteed.
                                                                                                                  


                                                                                                                  Interaction
                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                  The function complements the other variants for string extension in ara::core::BasicString. These include overloads for complete BasicString instances ([SWS_CORE_03076]) or their subranges ([SWS_CORE_03077]), C strings with length specification ([SWS_CORE_03078]) or as null-terminated pointers ([SWS_CORE_03079]), character repetitions ([SWS_CORE_03080]), iterator ranges ([SWS_CORE_03081]), initializer lists ([SWS_CORE_03082]), and separate StringView objects ([SWS_CORE_03308]).

                                                                                                                      The member function assign of class ara::core::BasicString serves to synchronously assign the content of an existing string to the calling instance according to the behavior of [basic.string] [SWS_CORE_03084]. The function is provided via header ara/core/string.h and accepts a const reference to a BasicString object (const BasicString &str). As return value, it returns a reference to the modified target object (*this), which enables method chaining [SWS_CORE_03084].
                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                      Regarding robustness, the function is explicitly specified as not exception safe [SWS_CORE_03084]. During dynamic memory allocations during the copy process, errors can occur that are not caught by exception guarantees; in case of error, the instance presumably remains in an undefined state. Specific AUTOSAR error codes or messages to DET or DEM are not provided for this assignment function.
                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                      In interplay with other interfaces, assign represents the copy variant within a family of assignment functions. While the moving overload [SWS_CORE_03085] is declared as conditionally exception safe, the remaining assignments—such as via substrings [SWS_CORE_03086], string views [SWS_CORE_03087], or iterator ranges [SWS_CORE_03091]—share the property not exception safe. Since thread safety is not specified, a concurrent call on the same instance without external synchronization is likely not reentrant and not data-safe.

Unlike other assignment functions such as [SWS_CORE_03086] or [SWS_CORE_03088], which trigger specific violations such as IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation and IsoStdLengthErrorViolation upon range or length violations and are considered not exception safe, this operation does not define any separate AUTOSAR violations.

                                                                                                                              The member function assign of class ara::core::BasicString ([SWS_CORE_03086]), provided via header ara/core/string.h, synchronously assigns a subrange of a passed source string str to the current instance. In addition to the source reference str, the call takes the start index pos and optionally the number of characters n, for which npos is defined by default. After the assignment, a reference to the modified object (*this) is returned. The functional semantics basically conform to the specifications from [basic.string] ([SWS_CORE_03086]).
                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                              In error handling, there is an explicit deviation from the ISO C++ standard: if condition pos > str.size() holds, no std::out_of_range is triggered, but a IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is caused ([SWS_CORE_03086]). In addition, the function is explicitly classified in the specification as not exception safe ([SWS_CORE_03086]).
                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                              Among the assignment methods of ara::core::BasicString, this substring overload complements the assignment of complete strings ([SWS_CORE_03084]), the conditionally exception-safe move assignment ([SWS_CORE_03085]), assignment from a StringView ([SWS_CORE_03087]), and operations with character buffers ([SWS_CORE_03088]) or iterator ranges ([SWS_CORE_03091]).

                                                                                                                                  use
                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                  The member function assign for StringView ([SWS_CORE_03087]) synchronously replaces the content of a ara::core::BasicString instance with the characters of the passed string view. The semantics follow the corresponding definition in [basic.string] of the C++ standard library. As return value, the function returns a reference to the modified target object (BasicString &), which enables chaining consecutive method calls. The declaration is provided via header file #include "ara/core/string.h".
                                                                                                                                  


                                                                                                                                  Error Handling and Exception Safety
                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                  The function is designated in the specification as not exception safe ([SWS_CORE_03087]). Interpretation: If the assignment requires increasing the internal buffer capacity and this memory allocation fails, an exception is likely thrown without any guarantee for the unchanged state of the instance.
                                                                                                                                  


                                                                                                                                  Concurrency and Limitations
                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                  Interpretation: Calls to assign on the same instance of ara::core::BasicString are not thread-safe and require external synchronization in the case of concurrent read or write access by multiple threads.
                                                                                                                                  


                                                                                                                                  Interaction
                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                  The function complements the assignment spectrum of ara::core::BasicString with type-safe views. It exists alongside the overloads for copy and move assignments ([SWS_CORE_03084], [SWS_CORE_03085]), substrings ([SWS_CORE_03086]), pointers to character data ([SWS_CORE_03088], [SWS_CORE_03089]), character repetitions ([SWS_CORE_03090]), iterator ranges ([SWS_CORE_03091]), and initializer lists ([SWS_CORE_03092]).

                                                                                                                                      use
                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                      The member function assign of class ara::core::BasicString synchronously assigns the first n characters from the passed character array s of type const value_type* to the current string instance and returns a reference to the modified object (*this) [SWS_CORE_03088]. The functional behavior basically conforms to the definition according to [basic.string], with AUTOSAR replacing the generic parameter type charT with value_type [SWS_CORE_03088].
                                                                                                                                      


                                                                                                                                      Error Handling and Boundary Conditions
                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                      The assignment is specified as not exception safe (not exception safe) [SWS_CORE_03088]. If the specified length n exceeds the maximum representable size max_size() (n > max_size()), the function triggers the AUTOSAR violation IsoStdLengthErrorViolation instead of std::length_error [SWS_CORE_03088]. Interpretation: The caller likely must ensure that s points to at least n valid characters, since the specification defines no separate buffer check.
                                                                                                                                      


                                                                                                                                      Interaction
                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                      The function is primarily suitable for non-null-terminated buffers or subranges of arrays. It complements the overload assign(const value_type* s) [SWS_CORE_03089], where the length is determined implicitly. In the class context of ara::core::BasicString, there are further assignment overloads for taking existing strings via copy [SWS_CORE_03084] or move [SWS_CORE_03085], for assigning substrings with index checking [SWS_CORE_03086], for adopting from StringView [SWS_CORE_03087], as well as for character repetitions [SWS_CORE_03090], iterator ranges [SWS_CORE_03091], and initializer lists [SWS_CORE_03092].

                                                                                                                                          The synchronous member function assign of class ara::core::BasicString ([SWS_CORE_03089]) from header ara/core/string.h replaces the current content of a string object with the passed character sequence s of type const value_type*. The call returns a reference to the modified object (*this). The functional behavior follows the specifications of the ISO C++ standard for [basic.string] with the documented deviation that character type charT is replaced by value_type ([SWS_CORE_03089]). Interpretation: Due to the lack of a separate length parameter, pointer s will likely point to a null-terminated character array.
                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                          With respect to error handling and robustness, the assignment function is classified as not exception safe (not exception safe) ([SWS_CORE_03089]). In contrast to related overloads such as assign(const BasicString&, size_type, size_type) ([SWS_CORE_03086]) or assign(const value_type*, size_type) ([SWS_CORE_03088]), no specific runtime violations such as IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation or IsoStdLengthErrorViolation are defined for this variant.
                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                          In module core, the function is part of a comprehensive overload family for content assignment. In addition to raw pointers, this also covers complete strings ([SWS_CORE_03084]), move semantics ([SWS_CORE_03085]), StringView instances ([SWS_CORE_03087]), repeated single characters ([SWS_CORE_03090]), iterator ranges ([SWS_CORE_03091]), and initializer lists ([SWS_CORE_03092]). AUTOSAR also provides similar assignment patterns in container types such as ara::core::Vector ([SWS_CORE_01328]).

                                                                                                                                              function assign [SWS_CORE_03090]
                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                              BasicString & assign (size_type n, value_type c);
                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                              As per corresponding usage in [basic.string] except for the following deviations: 1. charT replaced with value_type

  unreviewed
  Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 30dff2417cf7
  Provenance
  

                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                              use
                                                                                                                                              
  
                                                                                                                                              The member function assign of class ara::core::BasicString (defined in #include "ara/core/string.h") synchronously replaces the current content of the string with n consecutive copies of character c of type value_type [SWS_CORE_03090]. The semantics correspond to the specification for [basic.string] with the deviation that the type parameter charT is replaced by value_type [SWS_CORE_03090]. As return value, the function provides an lvalue reference to the modified instance (*this), enabling the chaining of further operations.
                                                                                                                                              

  
                                                                                                                                              Error Handling and Exception Safety
                                                                                                                                              
  
                                                                                                                                              According to the specification, the operation is explicitly classified as not exception safe [SWS_CORE_03090]. Unlike other overloads that trigger defined violations such as IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation [SWS_CORE_03086] or IsoStdLengthErrorViolation [SWS_CORE_03088] upon boundary violations, this function names no specific violations. If a required memory allocation fails, no assurances exist regarding the continuation of the previous object state.
                                                                                                                                              

  
                                                                                                                                              Concurrency and Limitations
                                                                                                                                              
  
                                                                                                                                              Since the assignment modifies the internal buffer directly and no internal synchronization is specified, concurrent access by multiple threads to the same instance will likely not be thread-safe (Interpretation). Concurrent calls must be coordinated externally by the caller.
                                                                                                                                              

  
                                                                                                                                              Interaction
                                                                                                                                              
  
                                                                                                                                              The function complements the assignment portfolio of ara::core::BasicString, which, in addition to copy and move assignments [SWS_CORE_03084], [SWS_CORE_03085] as well as iterators and initializer lists [SWS_CORE_03091], [SWS_CORE_03092], also provides interfaces for string views [SWS_CORE_03087]. A comparable assignment pattern with a repetition count exists analogously for ara::core::Vector::assign [SWS_CORE_01329].

                                                                                                                                                  function assign [SWS_CORE_03091]
                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                  template <class InputIterator> BasicString & assign (InputIterator first, InputIterator last);
                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                  As per corresponding usage in [basic.string]
                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                  
  AI-GENERATED
  unreviewed
  Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: cacec801ecc4
  Provenance
  

                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                  The template member function assign of class ara::core::BasicString synchronously replaces the content of the string with the elements of the range [first, last) according to the specifications in [basic.string] [SWS_CORE_03091]. It expects two input iterators as parameters and returns a reference to the modified instance (BasicString&) as return value [SWS_CORE_03091].
                                                                                                                                                  


                                                                                                                                                  Regarding error safety, the function is explicitly declared as not exception safe [SWS_CORE_03091]. In contrast to other overloads for which specific error checks such as IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation [SWS_CORE_03086] or IsoStdLengthErrorViolation [SWS_CORE_03088] are specified, the specification identifies no separate violations for this iterator range. If a memory allocation error occurs during the assignment, no exception guarantee exists.
                                                                                                                                                  


                                                                                                                                                  The specification makes no explicit statements regarding reentrancy and concurrency. In the event of competing read or write access by multiple threads to the same BasicString instance, the function is presumably not thread-safe and requires application-side synchronization.
                                                                                                                                                  


                                                                                                                                                  In the module, this interface complements the assignment operators and overloads for copy assignments [SWS_CORE_03084], conditionally exception-safe move assignments [SWS_CORE_03085], as well as assignments via StringView [SWS_CORE_03087] and std::initializer_list [SWS_CORE_03092]. AUTOSAR Adaptive also provides an equivalent iterator assignment for ara::core::Vector [SWS_CORE_01328].
                                                                                                                                                  


                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                  This usage note is based on the specification of AUTOSAR Adaptive R25-11.

                                                                                                                                                      function assign [SWS_CORE_03092]
                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                      BasicString & assign (std::initializer_list< value_type >);
                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                      As per corresponding usage in [basic.string] except for the following deviations: 1. charT replaced with value_type
                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                      
  AI-GENERATED
  unreviewed
  Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 5ed7cdcbec8f
  Provenance
  

                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                      The synchronous member function assign of class ara::core::BasicString ([SWS_CORE_03092]), defined in header file ara/core/string.h, replaces the previous content of the calling instance with the values of a passed std::initializer_list<value_type>. The functional behavior follows the requirements for [basic.string] of the ISO C++ standard entirely, with the only specific deviation that C++ standard type charT is replaced by value_type ([SWS_CORE_03092]). After successful assignment, the method returns a reference to the modified BasicString object itself ([SWS_CORE_03092]).
                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                      Classification not exception safe applies to execution ([SWS_CORE_03092]). In case of error, neither specific DET or DEM reports nor separate AUTOSAR violations are defined for this overload. This distinguishes the function from related overloads such as [SWS_CORE_03086], which triggers a IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation on an invalid position, or [SWS_CORE_03088], which reacts with a IsoStdLengthErrorViolation when max_size() is exceeded.
                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                      In the overall system of ara::core::BasicString, the function is closely related to alternative assignment interfaces. These include regular copy assignment ([SWS_CORE_03084]), conditionally exception-safe move assignment ([SWS_CORE_03085]), assignments via StringView ([SWS_CORE_03087]), pointers ([SWS_CORE_03089]), repetitions of single characters ([SWS_CORE_03090]), or iterator ranges ([SWS_CORE_03091]). In addition, sequence container ara::core::Vector also follows the same design pattern for initializer lists via [SWS_CORE_01330].
                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                      This usage note was automatically created based on AUTOSAR specification R25-11.

                                                                                                                                                          Regarding error handling, a specific deviation applies: if pos > sv.size() holds, an IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is thrown instead of std::out_of_range [SWS_CORE_03306].                                                                                                                                                           Constraints and interaction with related interfaces:
                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                            

                                                                                                                                                          • Interpretation: Since thread safety is not specified, concurrent read and write accesses to the same instance without external synchronization are likely not thread-safe.
                                                                                                                                                            •

                                                                                                                                                            •

                                                                                                                                                                  The member function at of class ara::core::BasicString ([SWS_CORE_03064]), provided via header #include "ara/core/string.h" ([SWS_CORE_03064]), grants synchronous access to a character at position pos and returns a mutable reference (reference) ([SWS_CORE_03064]). The basic semantics follow the standard [basic.string] ([SWS_CORE_03064]).
                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                  With regard to error handling, the implementation intentionally deviates from the C++ standard: If condition pos >= size() is met, the violation IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is thrown instead of a std::out_of_range exception ([SWS_CORE_03064]). Interpretation: An out-of-range violation in the AUTOSAR runtime system is likely to lead to termination or to the invocation of registered error routines via AddAbortHandler ([SWS_CORE_00054]).
                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                  Regarding concurrency and constraints, no thread safety is declared for the operation ([SWS_CORE_03064]).                                                                                                                                                                   For read access to constant instances, the overload const_reference at(size_type pos) const ([SWS_CORE_03063]) is available. The behavior on out-of-range access via IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation follows the consistent pattern of the Core types, as also specified for ara::core::Vector ([SWS_CORE_01355]), ara::core::Array ([SWS_CORE_01273]), ara::core::Map ([SWS_CORE_01456]), and ara::core::StringView ([SWS_CORE_02133]).
