                                                                                                                                                                                                      The member function clear of class ara::core::BasicString serves to clear the contents of a string instance according to the corresponding usage in [basic.string] [SWS_CORE_03057]. It is included via the header file #include "ara/core/string.h" [SWS_CORE_03057].
                                                                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                                                                      use
                                                                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                                                                      The operation has the signature void clear () noexcept;, accepts no parameters, and has no return value [SWS_CORE_03057]. The invocation occurs synchronously on the respective instance. Interpretation: Following the referenced semantics in [basic.string], the function is likely to remove all contained characters and reset the length of the string to zero.
                                                                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                                                                      Error handling
                                                                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                                                                      The function is classified as exception safe (exception safe) and declared with the specifier noexcept [SWS_CORE_03057]. No C++ exceptions are thrown. Specific error codes, DET, or DEM messages are not specified for this function [SWS_CORE_03057].
                                                                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                                                                      Interaction
                                                                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                                                                      In module core, container cleanup follows a uniform design pattern. The same semantics and signature are also found in ara::core::Vector::clear from ara/core/vector.h [SWS_CORE_01375] as well as in ara::core::Map::clear from ara/core/map.h [SWS_CORE_01485], which are likewise specified as synchronous, parameterless, and noexcept [SWS_CORE_03057] [SWS_CORE_01375] [SWS_CORE_01485].

                                                                                                                                                                                                          function compare [SWS_CORE_03321]
                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                          int compare (StringView sv) const noexcept;
                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                          As per corresponding usage in [basic.string]

  AI-GENERATED
  unreviewed
  Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 58e7a03ff5e0
  Provenance
  

                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                          use
                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Member function compare of class ara::core::BasicString ([SWS_CORE_03321]) serves for the synchronous, lexicographical comparison of the string content with a passed StringView sv. The functional semantics follow the C++ standard construct [basic.string] ([SWS_CORE_03321]). Interpretation: The return value of type int is negative if the string ranks lexicographically before sv, exactly 0 in case of equality, and positive if it ranks after sv.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          


                                                                                                                                                                                                          Error Handling and Exception Safety
                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                          The method is declared with noexcept and specified as exception-safe (exception safe) ([SWS_CORE_03321]). It throws no exceptions and reports errors neither via error codes nor via DET or DEM mechanisms.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          


                                                                                                                                                                                                          Concurrency and Limitations
                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Since it is a const operation (const) without modifying side effects on the instance state ([SWS_CORE_03321]), concurrent read calls from multiple execution contexts are likely thread-safe, provided no concurrent write accesses occur (interpretation).
                                                                                                                                                                                                          


                                                                                                                                                                                                          Interaction
                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                          While many data types in ara::core such as ErrorCode ([SWS_CORE_00571]) or Result ([SWS_CORE_00780]) rely on boolean equality operators, compare ([SWS_CORE_03321]) enables a three-way ordering check, comparable to the criteria of comparison objects like Map::value_compare ([SWS_CORE_01423]).

                                                                                                                                                                                                              function compare [SWS_CORE_03322]

                                                                                                                                                                                                              Member function compare of class ara::core::BasicString enables the synchronous lexicographical comparison of a substring with a string view ([SWS_CORE_03322]).
                                                                                                                                                                                                              


                                                                                                                                                                                                              Usage and Parameters
                                                                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                                                                              The method is called synchronously on an instance of ara::core::BasicString ([SWS_CORE_03322]). According to its signature, it accepts the following parameters:
                                                                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                                                                                

                                                                                                                                                                                                              • pos1: Start position of the sub-range to be compared in the calling string ([SWS_CORE_03322]).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                • 

                                                                                                                                                                                                              • n1: Maximum number of characters to compare ([SWS_CORE_03322]).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                • 

                                                                                                                                                                                                              • sv: The target string view of type StringView ([SWS_CORE_03322]).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                • 

                                                                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                                                                              The semantics follow the corresponding usage in [basic.string] ([SWS_CORE_03322]). The return value of type int is likely to yield zero upon equality and take on negative or positive values upon lexicographical deviation.
                                                                                                                                                                                                              


                                                                                                                                                                                                              Error Handling and Restrictions
                                                                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                                                                              Regarding exception handling, the function is classified as not exception safe ([SWS_CORE_03322]). Specific error codes as well as mechanisms such as DET or DEM are not identified in the specification. As a const-qualified member function, the call does not change the state of the instance ([SWS_CORE_03322]). The payload contains no explicit information regarding thread safety or reentrancy.
                                                                                                                                                                                                              


                                                                                                                                                                                                              Interaction
                                                                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                                                                              The function is available via header ara/core/string.h and complements the range of typed comparison operations in namespace ara::core, such as those defined for ErrorCode ([SWS_CORE_00571]) or Result ([SWS_CORE_00780]).
                                                                                                                                                                                                              


                                                                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                                                                              This usage note was created automatically based on the specification of the Core module (Release R25-11).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                  use
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                  The template member function compare of class ara::core::BasicString ([SWS_CORE_03323], header ara/core/string.h) serves for the synchronous lexicographical comparison of a section of the current instance with the sub-range of a passed object t. The behavior follows the definition of [basic.string] of the C++ standard [SWS_CORE_03323]. Parameters pos1 and n1 determine the start position and length of the sub-range of the calling instance, while pos2 and n2 specify the section of t to be compared.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                  The return value is a signed int value [SWS_CORE_03323] reflecting the relational order: it is less than zero if the own substring precedes, zero on equality, and greater than zero if it follows.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Error Handling and Boundary Conditions
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Regarding error handling, the function is specified as not exception safe [SWS_CORE_03323]; AUTOSAR-specific error codes, DET, or DEM messages do not exist for this operation. Interpretation: Callers must ensure beforehand that the indices are valid, since invalid range parameters are presumably likely to lead to undefined behavior in the absence of exception handling.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Interaction
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                  The method is declared as const [SWS_CORE_03323]. While basic operators such as operator== in ErrorCode ([SWS_CORE_00571]) or Result ([SWS_CORE_00780]) test for pure boolean equality, compare provides a three-way order relation over sub-ranges.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  


                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                  This usage note is based on the AUTOSAR Adaptive specification for Release R25-11.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Member function compare of class ara::core::BasicString ([SWS_CORE_03346]) serves for the synchronous, lexicographical comparison of a string with another instance str of type BasicString. The semantics follow the standardized usage in [basic.string] ([SWS_CORE_03346]). Interpretation: The returned integer value int is therefore likely to be 0 if both strings match, and less than or greater than 0 if the calling instance ranks lexicographically before or after parameter str, respectively.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Regarding error handling and exception safety, the function is declared as noexcept and explicitly classified as exception safe ([SWS_CORE_03346]). Specific error codes, return values for error signaling, or DET/DEM messages do not exist. A failure of the operation is ruled out during regular execution, since the comparison does not throw exceptions.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                      As a const-qualified method, the function does not modify the state of the object. Interpretation: Since the specification makes no explicit statements regarding thread safety, simultaneous read accesses by multiple threads to the same instance are likely safe, whereas concurrent modifying operations must be synchronized externally.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                      In the overall system of ara::core, the function joins relational comparison operations that are partly provided for other core types via equality operators, such as in [SWS_CORE_00137] for ErrorDomain, in [SWS_CORE_00571] for ErrorCode, and in [SWS_CORE_00780] for Result.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                          use
                                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Member function compare of class ara::core::BasicString synchronously compares a defined substring of the calling instance with another instance of type BasicString [SWS_CORE_03347]. Header ara/core/string.h serves for integration. Parameters pos1 and n1 define the start position and the maximum number of characters to compare, while str references the comparison string. The return value is an integer value (int), which indicates the lexicographical order: a value less than zero means that the own sub-segment precedes str, the value zero signals equality, and a value greater than zero indicates a subsequent positioning.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                          


                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Error Handling and Exception Safety
                                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                                          In the specification, the function is explicitly declared as not exception safe [SWS_CORE_03347]. Specific error codes, AUTOSAR return types such as ara::core::Result, or DET/DEM messages do not exist for this function. Since the behavior is modeled after ISO C++ clause [basic.string], a start position pos1 greater than the current string length is likely to result in an out-of-range exception.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                          


                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Concurrency and Limitations
                                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                                          As a const-qualified method, compare does not modify the state of its own string [SWS_CORE_03347]. Interpretation: Concurrent read calls from multiple threads on the same object are likely permissible as long as no competing write accesses occur. For concurrent modifications, the caller must ensure appropriate synchronization.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Method compare of class ara::core::BasicString ([SWS_CORE_03348]) performs a synchronous, three-way lexicographical comparison between substrings. The caller passes the start position and maximum length of its own instance (pos1, n1) as well as of the target string str (pos2, n2). The semantics thereby completely correspond to the behavior of std::basic_string::compare according to the ISO C++ standard [basic.string].
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                                                                                              The return value is a int with the following evaluation:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                

                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • A value less than 0 if the own substring is lexicographically before the passed one.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • 

                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • The value 0 if both substrings are identical.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • 

                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • A value greater than 0 if the own substring lexicographically follows.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • 

                                                                                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Regarding error handling and robustness, the function is declared as not exception safe according to the specification ([SWS_CORE_03348]). No AUTOSAR-specific error codes or DET entries exist. In case of erroneous index boundaries, such as when pos1 or pos2 exceed the respective string length, the function is likely to throw range errors such as std::out_of_range according to the C++ standard interpretation (Interpretation: adoption of the ISO C++ standard semantics).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                                                                                              The method is qualified as const ([SWS_CORE_03348]) and does not modify the involved instances. Although no explicit thread safety is specified, concurrent reading of the same object is likely to be non-critical provided that no concurrent write operations take place. In contrast to binary comparison operators such as for ara::core::ErrorCode ([SWS_CORE_00571]), compare enables a nuanced sorting order.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  use
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  The member function compare of class ara::core::BasicString from header #include "ara/core/string.h" serves for the synchronous lexicographical string comparison according to the behavior of [basic.string] [SWS_CORE_03349]. It compares the underlying string with the passed character sequence s of type const value_type* and returns an integer result of type int [SWS_CORE_03349]. Interpretation: The parameter s is likely to refer to a valid, null-terminated character array, with the return value presumably being negative if the own string is lexicographically smaller, zero on a match, and positive if it is greater.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Error Handling and Exception Safety
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  The specification explicitly designates the method as not exception safe [SWS_CORE_03349]. No no-throw guarantee exists, and any errors are not returned via structured types such as ara::core::ErrorCode. Specific platform error notifications such as DET or DEM messages are not intended for this call.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Concurrency and Interaction
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  In contrast to thread-safe comparison operators in module core, for instance for ErrorCode [SWS_CORE_00571], no thread safety is specified for compare [SWS_CORE_03349]. Since the member function is declared as const, concurrent read accesses to the same instance are likely to be non-critical as long as no conflicting modifications occur. Module core also defines comparison operators for domain and result types such as ErrorDomain [SWS_CORE_00137] or Result [SWS_CORE_00780], whereas compare specifically provides a three-way relational ordering for strings.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      The member function compare of class ara::core::BasicString ([SWS_CORE_03350]) synchronously compares a substring of the current instance with a null-terminated C-style string. The function is included via #include "ara/core/string.h". As parameters, it expects the start index pos1 (of type size_type), the maximum number of characters n1, and a pointer s of type const value_type*. The return value is an integer int value that reflects the lexicographical ordering relationship ([SWS_CORE_03350]).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      


                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      The function semantics are based on the behavior in [basic.string] with the specific difference that charT is replaced by value_type ([SWS_CORE_03350]). For error handling, no DET or DEM messages and no specific error codes are defined. Regarding exception safety, the function is explicitly classified as “not exception safe” ([SWS_CORE_03350]).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      


                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      With respect to concurrency, the method does not modify the internal state of the object as a const function. Interpretation: Concurrent read calls on the same object are likely to be possible without additional synchronization, as long as no conflicting write accesses occur. The caller must ensure that s points to a valid character array.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      


                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      In the overall system of ara::core, compare fits into the comparison mechanisms of the basic types, comparable to the equality and inequality operators for ara::core::ErrorCode ([SWS_CORE_00571]) or ara::core::Result ([SWS_CORE_00780]), but unlike simple operators, it provides a nuanced three-way evaluation for subranges.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The member function compare according to [SWS_CORE_03351] enables the lexicographical three-way comparison of a subsequence of the current instance of ara::core::BasicString with an external character array. The function is provided via the header file #include "ara/core/string.h" and is called as a synchronous, const member function (const).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The semantics follow the corresponding usage in the standard C++ section [basic.string], with charT being replaced by value_type ([SWS_CORE_03351]). The parameters define the subsequence of the calling instance to be compared via the start index pos1 and the length n1, as well as the external target array via the pointer s (of type const value_type*) and the number of characters to consider n2. The return value is an integer value (int) that returns zero on a match and negative or positive values upon lexicographical deviation.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Regarding failure safety, compare is specified as not exception safe ([SWS_CORE_03351]). The specification defines no specific DET or DEM messages; any error states with invalid indices or memory accesses are likely to be signaled via C++ exceptions in accordance with the referenced semantics of [basic.string]. Because no thread safety is declared, concurrent access to the same string requires external synchronization in the presence of concurrent write operations.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          In the context of the platform, compare serves for elementary string processing and forms a foundation for comparison and equality checks built on top of it, such as those implemented for other core data types like ara::core::Result or ara::core::ErrorCode via comparison operators.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              The synchronous member function copy from header file #include "ara/core/string.h" belongs to class ara::core::BasicString ([SWS_CORE_03410]). It copies a sub-sequence of up to n characters starting at position pos into destination memory s. Parameter pos has default value 0. As a return value, the function of type size_type provides the exact number of characters actually written. The behavior follows the definition of [basic.string] of the C++ standard, with the deviation that character type charT is replaced by value_type ([SWS_CORE_03410]).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              


                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              The following specifications apply to error handling and boundary conditions:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • Range checking: If the specified position lies past the end of the string (pos > size()), IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is raised instead of the standard exception std::out_of_range ([SWS_CORE_03410]).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • 

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • Exception safety: According to the specification, the operation is not exception-safe (not exception safe) ([SWS_CORE_03410]).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • 

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • Buffer capacity: Interpretation: The caller must ensure that the memory area addressed by s provides sufficient capacity for the characters to be written, as the interface does not validate destination buffer size.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • 

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              


                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              In module core, this function differs from the identically named method in ara::core::StringView ([SWS_CORE_02140]): While StringView::copy is declared as noexcept and specified as exception-safe, BasicString::copy provides no noexcept guarantee ([SWS_CORE_03410]).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  function crbegin [SWS_CORE_03049]

  Provenance
  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  According to [SWS_CORE_03049], the member function crbegin of class ara::core::BasicString synchronously returns a constant reverse iterator (const_reverse_iterator) to the last element of the string. The function takes no input parameters and follows the corresponding usage in the standard concept [basic.string].
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  The operation is specified as exception safe and provided with the identifier noexcept [SWS_CORE_03049], so that no exceptions are thrown at runtime. Specific error codes and mechanisms for error logging via DET or DEM are not provided in the specification.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Regarding concurrency and constraints, it should be noted that this is a non-modifying const method; concurrent read access to the same string instance is therefore likely to be thread-safe. During iteration, no modifying operations must be performed on the instance in order to avoid invalid iterators.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Within module core, the function ensures consistent semantics with further containers and utility classes:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • ara::core::Array according to [SWS_CORE_01260],
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • 

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • ara::core::Vector according to [SWS_CORE_01342],
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • 

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • ara::core::Map according to [SWS_CORE_01450],
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • 

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • ara::core::Span according to [SWS_CORE_01978], and
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • 

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • ara::core::StringView according to [SWS_CORE_02126].
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • 

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  In contrast to the implementations in Array, Span, and StringView, which are designated as constexpr, crbegin in BasicString as well as in Vector and Map is defined as a pure runtime method.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      function crend [SWS_CORE_03050]

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      use
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      The member function crend of class ara::core::BasicString is provided via header #include "ara/core/string.h" ([SWS_CORE_03050]). The call is performed synchronously and without parameters on an instance and returns a const_reverse_iterator. This iterator marks the end of a reverse iteration by pointing to the theoretical element immediately preceding the first character. The semantics correspond to the C++ Standard Library according to [basic.string] ([SWS_CORE_03050]).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      


                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Error handling
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      The method is declared as noexcept and specified as exception safe (exception safe) ([SWS_CORE_03050]). It throws no exceptions; specific error codes or reports to DET or DEM do not exist for this call.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      


                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Concurrency and Limitations
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Since crend is declared as const and does not modify the underlying object, concurrent read accesses across multiple threads are likely to be safe without synchronization (Interpretation: standard C++ container behavior). Concurrent write accesses to the same instance of ara::core::BasicString, on the other hand, require external synchronization, as modifications are likely to compromise the validity of iterators.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      


                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Interaction
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Within AUTOSAR Adaptive Core, crend integrates into a uniform iterator concept:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • ara::core::Array ([SWS_CORE_01261]) and ara::core::Vector ([SWS_CORE_01343]) provide identical reverse iterators for sequential containers.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • 

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • ara::core::Map ([SWS_CORE_01451]) offers the corresponding iteration boundary for associative data structures.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • 

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • ara::core::Span ([SWS_CORE_01979]) and ara::core::StringView ([SWS_CORE_02127]) implement analogous interfaces for non-owning views.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        •

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              function erase [SWS_CORE_03102]
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              BasicString & erase (size_type pos=0, size_type n=npos);

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              The synchronous member function erase of class ara::core::BasicString ([SWS_CORE_03102], declared in #include "ara/core/string.h") removes characters from a string. The call is performed on an instance specifying the start index pos (default value 0) and the maximum count to be removed n (default value npos). A reference to the modified object (BasicString &) is returned as the return value [SWS_CORE_03102]. The functioning follows the C++ standard [basic.string], with charT being replaced by value_type [SWS_CORE_03102].
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              


                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              With regard to error handling and boundary conditions, the following specifications apply:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • Range checking: If the start index is greater than the length of the string (pos > size()), the AUTOSAR violation IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is thrown instead of std::out_of_range [SWS_CORE_03102].
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • 

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • Exception safety: The operation is explicitly classified as not exception safe (not exception safe) [SWS_CORE_03102].
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • 

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • Concurrency: Since the function directly modifies the object and is not exception safe, concurrent unprotected access by multiple threads to the same instance is likely to lead to data inconsistencies.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • 

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              


                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              In interaction within the Core library, ara::core::BasicString provides iterator-based overloads in addition to this index-based variant: erase(const_iterator) for individual positions [SWS_CORE_03103] and erase(const_iterator, const_iterator) for ranges [SWS_CORE_03104]. Comparable interfaces for element removal across containers are also found in ara::core::Vector ([SWS_CORE_01372], [SWS_CORE_01373]) and in ara::core::Map ([SWS_CORE_01480] to [SWS_CORE_01483]).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  function erase [SWS_CORE_03103]
