                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Usage and signature
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              The member function insert of class ara::core::BasicString is provided via header #include "ara/core/string.h" [SWS_CORE_03098]. It takes an iterator p of type const_iterator and a character c of type value_type and returns a iterator [SWS_CORE_03098]. The functional semantics follow the definition in [basic.string], with charT replaced by value_type [SWS_CORE_03098]. Interpretation: The returned iterator likely points to the character newly inserted at position p.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              

  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Error Handling and Restrictions
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Regarding exception safety, the operation is declared as “not exception safe” [SWS_CORE_03098]. Specific error codes as well as messages to DET or DEM are not provided for in the specification; interpretation: if an error occurs during execution, there are likely no guarantees regarding the state of the string object.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              

  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Interplay with related containers
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              The pattern of insertion operations and the classification as “not exception safe” correspond to the standards of other containers in ara::core:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
    
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • In ara::core::Vector, positioned insert overloads exist for single values ([SWS_CORE_01367], [SWS_CORE_01368]), ranges ([SWS_CORE_01369], [SWS_CORE_01370]), and initializer lists ([SWS_CORE_01371]), which are likewise not exception-safe.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • 
    
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • In ara::core::Map, insert functions are specified for value pairs ([SWS_CORE_01460]) as well as positioned variants with iterator hint ([SWS_CORE_01463], [SWS_CORE_01469]), which are equally declared as not exception-safe.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                •

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Method insert of class ara::core::BasicString ([SWS_CORE_03099]) serves to synchronously insert multiple identical characters at a defined position of the string. Integration is done via header file #include "ara/core/string.h".
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Usage and Parameters
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  The call is made via the signature iterator insert(const_iterator p, size_type n, value_type c) according to the semantics of [basic.string], where charT is replaced by value_type ([SWS_CORE_03099]):
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • p: Iterator of the position (const_iterator) before which the content is inserted.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • 

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • n: Number of characters to insert (size_type).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • 

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • c: Character value of type value_type to be inserted.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • 

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  As return value, the function yields a iterator pointing to the first newly inserted character or position p, respectively.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Error Handling and Boundary Conditions
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  The specification explicitly classifies the operation as “not exception safe” ([SWS_CORE_03099]). Specific error codes, DET, or DEM messages are not defined in the payload. Interpretation: In the absence of an exception guarantee, a failure during required memory allocations is likely to immediately lead to an abortion of execution or an inconsistent state.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Interaction
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  The interface follows the general provision pattern of sequential AUTOSAR containers. A functionally equivalent overload for multiple insertion exists for ara::core::Vector ([SWS_CORE_01369]), which is likewise specified as not exception-safe. In contrast, associative containers such as ara::core::Map primarily use pair- or node-based interfaces ([SWS_CORE_01460], [SWS_CORE_01468]).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      The template function insert of class ara::core::BasicString ([SWS_CORE_03100]), declared in header ara/core/string.h, synchronously inserts a sequence defined by input iterators first and last into the string at iterator position p. The behavior as well as the returned iterator follow the corresponding definition in [basic.string] of the C++ standard library [SWS_CORE_03100].
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Regarding error handling, the function is explicitly classified as not exception safe [SWS_CORE_03100]. The specification provides neither specific error codes nor DET or DEM messages. If an error occurs during insertion—such as a failed memory allocation—the original state of the instance is unlikely to be restored and the operation presumably offers no transactional safety.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Regarding concurrency, the method is not reentrant on the same instance; concurrent accesses without external synchronization are likely to cause data races. In addition, existing iterators and references to the string are likely to become invalid due to possible reallocations or element shifts.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      This pattern corresponds to the uniform interface design of AUTOSAR Adaptive Core: range-based overloads of insert exist analogously for ara::core::Vector ([SWS_CORE_01370]) and ara::core::Map ([SWS_CORE_01466]), which are also based on the standard containers and are declared as not exception-safe.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Usage and Semantics
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The member function insert of class ara::core::BasicString inserts the content of an std::initializer_list<value_type> before the position designated by iterator p (of type const_iterator) and returns a iterator to the first inserted element [SWS_CORE_03101]. The declaration is provided via header ara/core/string.h [SWS_CORE_03101]. The functional semantics correspond to the specification in [basic.string] of the C++ standard library, where charT is replaced by value_type [SWS_CORE_03101].
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          


                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Error Handling and Exception Safety
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The specification defines no specific error codes, return values for error cases, or notifications to DET or DEM. Exception safety is explicitly specified as not exception safe [SWS_CORE_03101]. If an internal operation such as a memory allocation fails, the implementation grants no consistency guarantees for the state of the string.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          


                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Concurrency and Limitations
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The operation is executed synchronously in the context of the calling thread. Interpretation: Since the specification provides no internal synchronization mechanisms, concurrent modifying accesses to the same instance of ara::core::BasicString without external synchronization are likely not thread-safe.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          


                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Interplay in the module
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Inserting elements via initializer lists follows a consistent pattern in module core:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • ara::core::Vector offers an analogous insert function with iterator insert(const_iterator, std::initializer_list<T>) [SWS_CORE_01371] alongside overloads for single values and iterator ranges [SWS_CORE_01367] [SWS_CORE_01370].
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • 

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • ara::core::Map likewise provides a bulk insert operation via void insert(std::initializer_list<value_type>) [SWS_CORE_01467], which, like the string variant, is classified as not exception safe.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            •

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Member function insert of class ara::core::BasicString ([SWS_CORE_03310]) synchronously inserts the content of a string view (StringView sv) into the string at the specified index position (size_type pos). According to [SWS_CORE_03310], the semantics correspond to the specification in [basic.string]. The function returns a reference to the modified string (BasicString &), which allows chaining multiple operations.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              

  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              For usage, header #include "ara/core/string.h" must be included ([SWS_CORE_03310]). Regarding exception handling, the operation is explicitly specified as not exception-safe (not exception safe) ([SWS_CORE_03310]). If an error occurs during insertion or internal memory allocation, there are consequently no exception safety guarantees for the state of the object.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              

  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Regarding reentrancy and concurrency, the method is likely not thread-safe upon concurrent access to the same instance without external synchronization. This behavior corresponds to the other container operations in ara::core, where modifying insert functions like in ara::core::Vector ([SWS_CORE_01367], [SWS_CORE_01368], [SWS_CORE_01369], [SWS_CORE_01370], [SWS_CORE_01371]) and ara::core::Map ([SWS_CORE_01460], [SWS_CORE_01468]) are likewise defined as not exception-safe.



                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  function insert [SWS_CORE_03311]
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  template <class T> BasicString & insert (size_type pos1, const T &t, size_type pos2, size_type n=npos);
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  As per corresponding usage in [basic.string] except for the following deviations: 1. if ( pos1 > size() || pos2 > sv.size() ) IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is raised instead of std::out_of_range

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Usage and Call Context
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Template function insert of class ara::core::BasicString ([SWS_CORE_03311]) synchronously inserts a character sequence from object t into the existing string at position pos1. Via pos2 and the optional length specification n (defaulting to npos), the sub-range of t to be read is determined. As return value, the function yields a reference to the modified BasicString object (*this). The source object t is presumably interpreted here as std::string_view or a type-compatible character-like object, since the specification references sv.size().
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Error Handling and Exception Behavior
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  The function deliberately deviates from the ISO C++ standard regarding error handling: if pos1 exceeds the length of the destination string (pos1 > size()) or pos2 exceeds the length of the source range (pos2 > sv.size()), a IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is thrown instead of std::out_of_range ([SWS_CORE_03311]). The specification also classifies the function as not exception-safe (not exception safe) ([SWS_CORE_03311]), which is why retention of the original object state cannot be guaranteed in the event of memory errors.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Concurrency and Interaction
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  In the absence of an explicit reentrancy specification, unprotected parallel write or read accesses to the same instance are likely not thread-safe. In comparison to other core containers such as ara::core::Vector ([SWS_CORE_01367]) or ara::core::Map ([SWS_CORE_01460]), whose insert functions operate iterator-based and are also considered not exception-safe, BasicString::insert operates index-based and integrates the AUTOSAR-specific violations concept ([SWS_CORE_03311]).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  The member function pop_back of ara::core::BasicString ([SWS_CORE_03105]) is provided via the header #include "ara/core/string.h". It has the signature void pop_back(), takes no input parameters, and yields no return value. According to the specification, the behavior corresponds to the corresponding use in [basic.string] ([SWS_CORE_03105]). Interpretation: In accordance with [basic.string], the operation is likely to remove the last character synchronously from the string.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  With regard to error handling and robustness, the function is classified as not exception safe ([SWS_CORE_03105]). Specific error codes or diagnostic messages such as DET or DEM are not defined for this interface. The caller must ensure before execution that the string has a valid state and is not empty, since exception safety is not guaranteed in the event of an error.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  In module core, an analogous interaction exists for sequential data structures: The class ara::core::Vector from ara/core/vector.h also provides a member function pop_back ([SWS_CORE_01365]). This follows the corresponding use in [vector] and exhibits the same restriction regarding exception safety with the classification not exception safe ([SWS_CORE_01365]).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      use
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Function push_ (with signature void push_back (value_type c);) belongs to class ara::core::BasicString and serves for synchronously appending a character c of type value_type to an existing string [SWS_CORE_03083]. The declaration is provided via header file #include "ara/core/string.h" [SWS_CORE_03083]. Technically, the functionality is aligned with the corresponding usage of the C++ standard construct [basic.string] [SWS_CORE_03083].
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Error handling
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      The specification defines no specific error codes, return values, or diagnostic messages for the element, since the return is void [SWS_CORE_03083]. Regarding exception safety, the operation is explicitly classified as not exception safe [SWS_CORE_03083].
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Concurrency and Limitations
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Since the state of the instance is modified by appending the character and no synchronization mechanisms are specified, a concurrent call on the same instance without external protection is unlikely to be thread-safe. Calling software components must therefore coordinate access themselves if needed.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The member function replace of class ara::core::BasicString ([SWS_CORE_03106], declared in #include "ara/core/string.h") synchronously replaces a subrange of the current string starting at index pos1 with a length of n1 characters with the content of the passed BasicString str. The semantics follow the corresponding definition in [basic.string] of the C++ standard library [SWS_CORE_03106]. A reference to the modified object (BasicString &) is returned, enabling method chaining [SWS_CORE_03106].
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Regarding error handling and exception safety, the function is explicitly classified as not exception safe [SWS_CORE_03106]. If an error occurs during execution—such as insufficient memory—the operation does not guarantee a defined initial state. Unlike variants such as [SWS_CORE_03107] or [SWS_CORE_03108], which specify specific AUTOSAR violations like IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation or IsoStdLengthErrorViolation, this overload refers directly to the standard semantics [SWS_CORE_03106].
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Regarding concurrency, it can be assumed (interpretation) that modifying accesses to the same BasicString instance are not thread-safe and must be synchronized externally. For different replacement scenarios, related overloads are available: replacements with substrings via position specifications ([SWS_CORE_03107]), using pointers to C strings ([SWS_CORE_03108], [SWS_CORE_03109]), with StringView ([SWS_CORE_03312]), or via iterator ranges ([SWS_CORE_03111]).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              function replace [SWS_CORE_03107]
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              BasicString & replace (size_type pos1, size_type n1, const BasicString &str, size_type pos2, size_type n2=npos);
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              As per corresponding usage in [basic.string] except for the following deviations: 1. charT replaced with value_type 2. if ( pos > max_size() || pos2 > str.size() ) IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is raised instead of std::out_of_range
