                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The template member function replace of class ara::core::BasicString ([SWS_CORE_03313], declared in ara/core/string.h) replaces a subrange of the string synchronously with a section of the object t. The range to be replaced is determined by the start position pos1 and the character count n1. The range to be inserted is determined by index pos2 as well as the maximum length n2, which is assigned npos by default ([SWS_CORE_03313]). As return value, the function returns a reference to the modified instance. Interpretation: The type T is likely to be a type compatible with StringView, as the specification checks the validity of pos2 against sv.size().
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The semantics follow the ISO standard [basic.string], but define two specific deviations ([SWS_CORE_03313]):
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The character type charT is replaced by value_type.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • 

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • If pos1 > size() or pos2 > sv.size() holds, the violation IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is thrown instead of std::out_of_range.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • 

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Regarding exception safety, the function is considered not exception safe ([SWS_CORE_03313]). In the module context, the method complements related overloads such as directly passing a BasicString with a subrange ([SWS_CORE_03107]), replacement via StringView ([SWS_CORE_03312], [SWS_CORE_03314]), and operations based on pointers ([SWS_CORE_03108]).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Usage and Semantics
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              The member function replace of class ara::core::BasicString ([SWS_CORE_03314]) synchronously replaces the character range bounded by iterators i1 and i2 with the content of the passed StringView sv. The function is provided via header file #include "ara/core/string.h" and returns a reference to the modified instance (*this) ([SWS_CORE_03314]). Semantically, the operation follows the specification of [basic.string] of the C++ standard ([SWS_CORE_03314]).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              

  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Error Handling and Boundary Conditions
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              The operation is explicitly classified in the specification as "not exception safe" ([SWS_CORE_03314]). While related index-based variants such as [SWS_CORE_03107] or [SWS_CORE_03313] explicitly trigger a IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation in case of out-of-range conditions, this overload defines no separate violations. Interpretation: The passed iterators i1 and i2 presumably must represent a valid range within the target instance to avoid undefined behavior. Since modifications are made directly to the object and no exception safety is guaranteed ([SWS_CORE_03314]), concurrent access without external synchronization is likely not thread-safe.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              

  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Interplay in the module
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              The signature fits into the family of replacement functions of BasicString. It represents the iterator-based counterpart to index-based replacement using StringView ([SWS_CORE_03312]) and complements the other iterator-based overloads for strings ([SWS_CORE_03111]), character arrays ([SWS_CORE_03112], [SWS_CORE_03406]), iterator ranges ([SWS_CORE_03411]), and initializer lists ([SWS_CORE_03413]).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  The synchronous member function replace of class ara::core::BasicString ([SWS_CORE_03406]), declared in header file #include "ara/core/string.h", replaces the subrange of the string defined by iterator pair [i1, i2) with the character sequence s. As a return value, the method returns a reference to the calling instance (BasicString&), which allows chaining further string operations. The functional semantics follow the definition in [basic.string], with the parameter type charT being replaced by value_type as a deviation ([SWS_CORE_03406]).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  With regard to execution safety, the function is explicitly specified as not exception safe (not exception safe) ([SWS_CORE_03406]). In contrast to overloads with index and position specifications such as [SWS_CORE_03107] or [SWS_CORE_03108], which explicitly define a IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation or IsoStdLengthErrorViolation on out-of-bounds errors, [SWS_CORE_03406] specifies no AUTOSAR-specific violations. It is therefore presumably the responsibility of the caller to ensure that [i1, i2) represents a valid iterator range within the string and pointer s refers to a properly terminated character sequence.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  The function complements the range of replacement operations of BasicString in interaction with related interfaces:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
    
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • For iterator-based replacement by a fixed number of n characters from a pointer, overload [SWS_CORE_03112] exists.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • 
    
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • If another BasicString object or a StringView is to be used as source instead, [SWS_CORE_03111] or [SWS_CORE_03314] are available.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • 
    
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • If position-based indices (size_type) are preferred over iterators, developers can resort to overloads such as [SWS_CORE_03106] or [SWS_CORE_03109].
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • 
    
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • [SWS_CORE_03411] and [SWS_CORE_03413] serve for replacement by generic iterator ranges or initializer lists.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    •

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      use
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      The synchronous template member function replace of class ara::core::BasicString from header ara/core/string.h replaces the subrange of a string defined by the iterator pair [i1, i2) with the character sequence of the input range [j1, j2) of an arbitrary InputIterator [SWS_CORE_03411]. The behavior follows the semantics of [basic.string] and returns a reference to the modified object (*this), thereby enabling chained method calls [SWS_CORE_03411].
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      


                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Error Handling and Exception Safety
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      The operation is explicitly specified as not exception safe (not exception safe) [SWS_CORE_03411]. Unlike position-based overloads such as [SWS_CORE_03107], [SWS_CORE_03108], or [SWS_CORE_03313], where out-of-range accesses lead to violation IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation or IsoStdLengthErrorViolation, no specific violations are defined for this iterator variant [SWS_CORE_03411].
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      


                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Concurrency and Interaction
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Since the module standard specifies no mechanisms for internal synchronization, concurrent write or read access by multiple threads to the same instance is likely not to be thread-safe without external locking (Interpretation). The function joins a family of iterator-based replacements that also includes variants for BasicString [SWS_CORE_03111], StringView [SWS_CORE_03314], character arrays [SWS_CORE_03112], [SWS_CORE_03406], initializer lists [SWS_CORE_03413], and character repetitions [SWS_CORE_03414]. For position-based replacements, alternatives such as [SWS_CORE_03106] are available.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The member function replace of class ara::core::BasicString ([SWS_CORE_03413]), provided in header ara/core/string.h, synchronously replaces a character range bounded by two const_iterator with the elements of an std::initializer_list<value_type>. As return value, it delivers a reference to the modified BasicString object ([SWS_CORE_03413]). The functional behavior corresponds to the C++ standard requirement [basic.string], where the character type charT is replaced by value_type ([SWS_CORE_03413]).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          With regard to error and exception handling, the function is classified as not exception safe ([SWS_CORE_03413]). Unlike index-based variants for which specific runtime violations such as IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation or IsoStdLengthErrorViolation are defined ([SWS_CORE_03107], [SWS_CORE_03108], [SWS_CORE_03313]), this iterator-based overload names no AUTOSAR violations. Because the specification does not provide for synchronization mechanisms, concurrent modifying access to the same string instance is presumably not thread-safe.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The operation complements the spectrum of iterator-based replacement methods for whole strings ([SWS_CORE_03111]), pointers with length specification ([SWS_CORE_03112]), string pointers ([SWS_CORE_03406]), StringView ([SWS_CORE_03314]), iterator ranges ([SWS_CORE_03411]), and character repetitions ([SWS_CORE_03414]). In addition, index- and position-based overloads exist ([SWS_CORE_03106], [SWS_CORE_03109], [SWS_CORE_03110], [SWS_CORE_03312]).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              The member function replace of class ara::core::BasicString ([SWS_CORE_03414]), provided via header file #include "ara/core/string.h", replaces the subrange of the string bounded by the iterator pair i1 and i2 with n consecutive copies of character c of type value_type. The behavior corresponds to the standardized semantics from [basic.string], where charT is substituted by value_type according to the AUTOSAR deviation ([SWS_CORE_03414]). As return value, the synchronous call returns a reference to the modified BasicString object ([SWS_CORE_03414]).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              

  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Regarding error handling, the function is classified as not exception safe ([SWS_CORE_03414]). In contrast to index-based overloads such as [SWS_CORE_03107] or [SWS_CORE_03108], which trigger specific runtime errors such as IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation or IsoStdLengthErrorViolation in the event of range or length errors, [SWS_CORE_03414] names no violations. Interpretation: Callers must presumably ensure the validity of the iterator range spanned by i1 and i2 themselves, since invalid ranges will likely lead to undefined behavior in the absence of exception safety.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              

  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              In interaction with other overloads of the class, [SWS_CORE_03414] forms the iterator-based counterpart to the index-based function [SWS_CORE_03110] (replacement of n1 characters starting from index pos with n2 characters c). Further iterator-based alternatives allow replacement with a BasicString object ([SWS_CORE_03111]), a character array with length specification ([SWS_CORE_03112]), a null-terminated string ([SWS_CORE_03406]), a StringView ([SWS_CORE_03314]), an iterator pair ([SWS_CORE_03411]), or an initializer list ([SWS_CORE_03413]).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  The synchronous member function reserve of class ara::core::BasicString ([SWS_CORE_03054]) serves in module core for capacity reservation of strings. It is included via header file <ara/core/string.h> and generally follows the semantics of the ISO C++ standard for [basic.string]. The call takes place via the signature void reserve(size_type res_arg=0), where parameter res_arg is defaulted to 0 and no value is returned [SWS_CORE_03054].
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Regarding error handling, the specification defines an explicit deviation from the standard behavior of C++:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
    
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • If the requested memory value exceeds the maximum size (res_arg > max_size()), IsoStdLengthErrorViolation is raised instead of std::length_error [SWS_CORE_03054].
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • 
    
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • The description of the content of this violation corresponds to the definition of std::length_error [SWS_CORE_03054].
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • 
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  As a restriction regarding exception safety, the function is explicitly classified as not exception safe [SWS_CORE_03054]. This approach corresponds to the method reserve of container class ara::core::Vector from <ara/core/vector.h> ([SWS_CORE_01347]), which likewise relies on IsoStdLengthErrorViolation for invalid capacity requests.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      The synchronous member function resize of ara::core::BasicString ([SWS_CORE_03058]) adjusts the length of the string to the specified number of elements sz. It is based on the semantics of the C++ standard type [basic.string], but exhibits AUTOSAR-specific peculiarities with regard to error handling.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Error Handling and Exception Safety
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      If the requested size sz exceeds the maximum value max_size(), deviating from std::basic_string, no std::length_error is generated, but a IsoStdLengthErrorViolation is triggered ([SWS_CORE_03058]). In the specification, the operation is explicitly declared as not exception safe ([SWS_CORE_03058]). If an internal memory allocation or enlargement fails, the state of the object will likely remain Interpretation: undefined or inconsistent, which is why callers should perform size checks in advance.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Interaction and related interfaces
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • For targeted filling during an enlargement, ara::core::BasicString provides the overload resize(size_type, value_type) ([SWS_CORE_03059]).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • 

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • The container class ara::core::Vector exhibits an analogous behavior: its methods [SWS_CORE_01350] and [SWS_CORE_01351] likewise trigger max_size() when IsoStdLengthErrorViolation is exceeded and similarly offer no exception guarantee.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        •



                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          function resize [SWS_CORE_03059]
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          void resize (size_type sz, value_type c);

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The synchronous member function resize of class ara::core::BasicString (declared in header ara/core/string.h, [SWS_CORE_03059]) adjusts the number of contained characters to the target size sz. If the string is enlarged, additional characters are filled with the passed character c of type value_type. The semantics follow the definition in [basic.string] of the C++ standard, but differ in that charT is replaced by value_type ([SWS_CORE_03059]).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          With regard to error handling and boundary conditions, the following specifications apply:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            
    
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Violations: If sz > max_size() holds, IsoStdLengthErrorViolation is triggered. This replaces the standard throwing of std::length_error ([SWS_CORE_03059]).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • 
    
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Exception safety: The operation is declared as not exception safe ([SWS_CORE_03059]). Error states such as size violations will therefore likely lead directly to termination on the platform side instead of throwing regular C++ exceptions.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • 
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The method complements the functional overload resize(size_type sz) within ara::core::BasicString ([SWS_CORE_03058]). The same strategy regarding IsoStdLengthErrorViolation when exceeding the maximum length is also used by the container methods of ara::core::Vector, namely resize(size_type sz) ([SWS_CORE_01350]) and resize(size_type sz, const T &c) ([SWS_CORE_01351]).
